name: BQ25895RTWR
title: I2C-controlled single-cell 5 A switch-mode charger with power path, USB detection and 3.1 A boost
summary: A single-cell Li-ion and Li-polymer charger built around a 1.5 MHz synchronous buck converter that charges at up to 5 A from a 3.9 V to 14 V input. It has a narrow-VDC power path with an 11 mΩ battery FET, USB BC1.2 and MaxCharge adapter detection on D+/D–, an input current optimizer, and a 4.55 V to 5.55 V boost mode that can source 3.1 A from the battery out of PMID. Every setting is reachable over I2C, a 7-bit ADC reports the input, battery and system voltages, TS and charge current, and the part also charges on its own from register defaults.

pins.name: VBUS
pins.function: Charger input. The internal reverse-blocking N-FET (RBFET) runs from VBUS (its source) to PMID. Bypassed to PGND right at the IC by 1 µF ceramic.

pins.name: D+
pins.function: USB data line, positive. Used for USB host and charging-port detection: BC1.2 data contact detection, primary and secondary detection, and the MaxCharge adjustable high-voltage adapter handshake.

pins.name: D-
pins.function: USB data line, negative. Same detection role as D+.

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Open-drain charge status, pulled up through 10 kΩ. Low while charging; high when charging is done or turned off; toggles at 1 Hz on a fault. STAT_DIS turns it off.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock; 10 kΩ pull-up to the logic rail.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data; 10 kΩ pull-up to the logic rail.

pins.name: INT
pins.function: Open-drain interrupt, 10 kΩ pull-up to a logic rail. Sends an active-low 256 µs pulse to report status changes and faults.

pins.name: OTG
pins.function: Boost enable. Boost mode runs when OTG is high, OTG_CONFIG = 1 and no source is present on VBUS.

pins.name: CE
pins.function: Charge enable, active low. Charging runs with CHG_CONFIG = 1 and CE low. Must be driven or tied high or low, never left open.

pins.name: ILIM
pins.function: Input current limit set by a resistor to ground: the pin is regulated at 0.8 V and IINMAX = KILIM / RILIM. The lower of this limit (with EN_ILIM high) and IINLIM applies. The pin cannot set a limit under 500 mA. Below 0.8 V the pin voltage is proportional to input current: IIN = KILIM × VILIM / (RILIM × 0.8). EN_ILIM = 0 turns the pin off.

pins.name: TS
pins.function: Battery temperature input. An NTC thermistor plus a divider from REGN to TS to GND set the temperature window; charging pauses when TS leaves the window. The thermistor named is a 103AT-2.

pins.name: QON
pins.function: BATFET enable and reset input with an internal pull-up. In ship mode, low for tSHIPMODE turns the BATFET on. With no VBUS, low for tQON_RST turns the BATFET off for tBATFET_RST and back on, a full system power reset.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Battery positive terminal. The internal BATFET runs from BAT to SYS. 10 µF close to the pin.

pins.name: SYS
pins.function: System output. The internal BATFET runs from BAT to SYS. When the battery is below the minimum system voltage the converter holds SYS at that minimum. 20 µF close to the pin.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Power ground of the converter; the source of the low-side N-FET. Tied straight to the ground side of the input and output capacitors, with one connection to analog ground close to the PGND pins.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node to the inductor: source of the high-side N-FET and drain of the low-side N-FET. A 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor runs from SW to BTST.

pins.name: BTST
pins.function: High-side gate driver supply; the anode of the internal bootstrap diode. 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor from SW to BTST.

pins.name: REGN
pins.function: Low-side driver supply from the internal LDO; the cathode of the bootstrap diode. 4.7 µF, 10 V ceramic to analog ground close to the IC. Also biases the TS divider.

pins.name: PMID
pins.function: Boost output, at the drains of the RBFET and the HSFET. Without OTG, at least 8.2 µF to PGND; with OTG, at least 40 µF for up to 2.4 A out and 60 µF for up to 3.1 A.

pins.name: DSEL
pins.function: Open-drain D+/D– multiplexer select, floating with a 10 kΩ pull-up. Pulled low while input source detection runs and the IC needs D+ and D–; stays low when MaxCharge is found; floats high for every other source type.

pins.name: PowerPAD
pins.function: Exposed pad for heat. Always soldered, with vias in the pad joining PGND and the ground plane.

circuits.title: D+/D– interface and 2.4 A boost output
circuits.description: One USB input feeds VBUS, with D+ and D– wired straight to the connector so the charger can identify the port and run the high-voltage adapter handshake. The buck stage drives SYS through a 2.2 µH inductor into two 10 µF capacitors, and the battery on BAT is charged at up to 5 A. A 260 Ω resistor on ILIM sets the hardware input limit to about 1.5 A. PMID carries 40 µF and is the 5 V boost output for a phone, rated to 2.4 A. The host talks over I2C, reads INT and drives OTG and /CE; SDA, SCL and INT are pulled up to the host rail. A divider from REGN with a 10 kΩ pack NTC on TS gives the temperature window, STAT drives an LED fed from SYS, and an optional button on QON gives ship-mode exit and system reset. DSEL is unused.

operation.text: Four N-channel FETs are inside: Q1 the reverse-blocking FET from VBUS to PMID, Q2 the high-side switch from PMID to SW, Q3 the low-side switch from SW to PGND, and Q4 the BATFET from SYS to BAT. The bootstrap diode for the high-side driver is inside too.

Bias comes from whichever of VBUS and BAT is higher. Once VBUS passes VVBUS_UVLOZ or BAT passes VBAT_UVLOZ, the sleep and battery-depletion comparators and the BATFET driver wake, every register returns to its default, and the I2C port answers.

With no input and the battery above VBAT_DPLZ, the BATFET connects the battery to SYS while REGN stays off to keep quiescent current low. Discharge current through the BATFET is watched; above IBATFET_OCP the BATFET opens at once and BATFET_DIS is set, and it stays off until an input arrives or one of the BATFET-enable events occurs.

On plug-in the steps run in order: REGN LDO up, poor-source check, D+/D– source detection (when AUTO_DPDM_EN is set) to load IINLIM, VINDPM threshold set, then the converter starts. REGN comes up when VBUS is above VVBUS_UVLOZ, above VBAT + VSLEEPZ in buck mode (or below VBAT + VSLEEP in boost mode), and 220 ms have passed; otherwise the part sits in high impedance with REGN off, drawing under IVBUS_HIZ, while the battery runs the system.

Before the buck starts, VBUS must be below VACOV and must stay above VVBUSMIN while IBADSRC (30 mA typ) is drawn. A source that passes sets VBUS_GD and pulses INT; one that fails is retried every 2 s.

Detection follows USB BC1.2 to tell SDP, CDP and DCP apart, then non-standard adapters by their D+/D– divider voltages once the 500 ms data-contact timer runs out. When a DCP is found and MAXC_EN or HVDCP_EN is set, the MaxCharge handshake asks the adapter to raise its output from 5 V to 9 V or 12 V. At the end INT pulses, IINLIM is loaded, PG_STAT is set and SDP_STAT updated. The host may overwrite IINLIM afterwards; the lower of IINLIM and the ILIM pin always applies, ICO or not. With AUTO_DPDM_EN clear, detection is skipped and IINLIM, VBUS_STAT and SDP_STAT keep their old values. In host mode, setting FORCE_DPDM reruns detection; the bit clears itself when done.

The input voltage limit spans 3.9 V to 14 V. With FORCE_VINDPM = 1 the host writes an absolute threshold to VINDPM. With FORCE_VINDPM = 0 (default) the part computes the threshold itself from VINDPM_OS and VINDPM is read-only. INT pulses once the threshold is set.

After the input limit is set the converter starts; the BATFET opens if charging is off, otherwise stays on. While SYS is below 2.2 V the input limit is held to the lower of 200 mA and IINLIM; above 2.2 V it is the lower of the ILIM pin and IINLIM (ICO_EN = 0) or IDPM_LIM (ICO_EN = 1). The buck runs at a fixed 1.5 MHz with type III compensation suited to ceramic output capacitors, and its ramp scales with PMID to keep loop gain constant over input voltage. At light load, when the battery is below the minimum system voltage or charging is off, it changes to PFM, with duty set by the SYS to VBUS ratio.

ICO finds the highest input current the source can give without its voltage falling to VINDPM. It is on by default (ICO_EN = 1) and runs after a DCP or MaxCharge source is detected; FORCE_ICO runs it for any source. The limit in use is reported in IDPM_LIM while ICO is on, and is IINLIM when it is off; either way the ILIM pin caps it unless EN_ILIM = 0.

Boost delivers battery power out through PMID, up to 3.1 A. It starts when BAT is above BATLOWV, VBUS is below BAT + VSLEEP, OTG is high with OTG_CONFIG = 1, TS is inside the boost temperature window set by BHOT and BCOLD, and 30 ms have passed. The switching frequency is 500 kHz or 1.5 MHz by BOOST_FREQ; writes to BOOST_FREQ are ignored while OTG_CONFIG is set. VBUS_STAT reads 111 in boost; the output defaults to 5 V, set by BOOSTV, and holds while BAT stays above VOTG_BAT.

The BATFET separates SYS from the battery. SYS is held at or above the SYS_MIN setting (3.5 V default) even with a flat battery: below that, the BATFET runs linear; above it, the BATFET is fully on and SYS sits one BATFET drop above BAT. VSYS_STAT is high during minimum-system regulation.

When the source is overloaded, either its current reaches IINLIM or IDPM_LIM or its voltage falls to VINDPM, charge current is cut until the input is back inside both limits. If charge current has reached zero and the source is still overloaded, SYS falls; once it drops below the battery, supplement mode starts and the battery helps carry the load. VDPM_STAT and IDPM_STAT show which limit is active.

When SYS falls below BAT the BATFET turns on, its gate regulated so that VDS stays at 30 mV at low current, which avoids chattering in and out of the mode. As discharge current rises the gate drive rises until the BATFET is fully on, after which VDS grows linearly with current. The BATFET turns off to leave supplement mode when the battery falls below the depletion threshold.

With CHG_CONFIG = 1 and CE low, the part runs a full charge cycle on its own using the defaults of Table 8-4; the host may change any of them over I2C. A cycle starts when the converter is running, charging is enabled with ICHG not 0 mA, TS shows no fault, the safety timer has not expired and BATFET_DIS = 0. The charge ends when current falls below the termination level with the battery above the recharge threshold, outside DPM and thermal regulation. A battery that then drops below the recharge threshold (VRECHG) starts a new cycle; toggling CE or CHG_CONFIG also starts one. CHRG_STAT reads 00 not charging, 01 precharge, 10 fast charge (CC or CV phase), 11 done, and INT pulses at the end of a cycle.

Below 2 V the battery gets IBATSHORT (100 mA); from 2 V to 3 V the precharge current (128 mA default, 64 mA to 1024 mA); above 3 V the fast-charge current (2048 mA default, up to 5056 mA) followed by constant voltage at VREG (3.84 V to 4.608 V). In DPM or thermal regulation the current can fall short of the setting; termination is then suspended and the safety timer runs at half speed.

At termination the BATFET turns off while the converter keeps powering SYS; the BATFET can still turn on for supplement mode. CHRG_STAT goes to 11 and INT pulses. Termination waits while input current, input voltage or thermal regulation is active, and EN_TERM = 0, written before termination, turns it off.

Resistance between the charger and the cell (traces, connector, FETs, sense resistor) moves charging from constant current into constant voltage too soon. IRCOMP raises the regulation voltage by charge current times BAT_COMP, up to VCLAMP, lengthening the constant-current phase. The host sets VCLAMP and BAT_COMP for safe operation.

TS is compared with fractions of REGN. A cycle may start only with TS between VLTF and VHTF; once running, charging continues while TS stays between VLTF and VTCO, otherwise it pauses until TS is back between VLTF and VHTF. A TS fault is reported in REG0C[2:0], pulses INT, and STAT flags it while charging is paused.

In boost mode the battery must stay between VBCOLDx and VBHOTx (cold –10°C or –20°C; hot 55°C, 60°C or 65°C) unless BHOT = 11 turns the check off. Outside the window boost and the BATFET turn off and BATFET_DIS is set to cut PMID leakage; once back in range, clearing BATFET_DIS or a low-to-high edge on QON restores them.

Below VBATLOWV the timer is 4 hours; the fast-charge timer is set by CHG_TIMER. On expiry CHRG_FAULT reads 11 and INT pulses. EN_TIMER turns the timer off. During input voltage, input current or thermal regulation it counts at half rate (a 5 hour setting lasts 10 hours if the whole charge is in input current regulation) unless TMR2X_EN = 0.

The ADC reports VBUS, battery voltage, system voltage, TS as a fraction of REGN, and charge current in REG0E to REG12. In one-shot mode (CONV_RATE = 0, default) setting CONV_START starts a conversion; the bit clears when the result is ready, within tCONV (1 s max). In continuous mode (CONV_RATE = 1) a result comes every second until CONV_RATE is cleared. The ADC turns REGN on, which raises quiescent current. On battery alone it runs only with VBAT above the SYS_MIN setting.

INT gives a 256 µs low pulse when a source is identified, a good source is found (VBUS above the battery, below VACOV and above VVBUSMIN with IBADSRC drawn), the input is removed, charging completes, or any REG0C fault occurs. A fault is latched in REG0C until read, and no new fault pulse is sent until then; reading REG0C twice gives first the latched and then the present state.

Setting BATFET_DIS turns the BATFET off, at once or after tSM_DLY when BATFET_DLY = 1, leaving SYS unpowered and battery drain minimal. The BATFET returns on adapter plug-in, on clearing BATFET_DIS, on REG_RST, or on a high-to-low edge on QON held for tSHIPMODE.

With no input and BATFET_DIS = 0, holding QON low for tQON_RST opens the BATFET for tBATFET_RST and closes it again, a power-on reset of everything on SYS without the host. BATFET_RST_EN = 0 turns this off.

For adapters that change voltage on VBUS current pulses, set EN_PUMPX, then one of PUMPX_UP or PUMPX_DN, never both. The input limit then toggles between IINLIM or IDPM_LIM and the 100 mA level; the bit stays set during the sequence and clears at its end. Clearing EN_PUMPX aborts the sequence and restores the limit at once; with EN_PUMPX low, writes to PUMPX_UP and PUMPX_DN do nothing.

ILIM is held at 0.8 V; above that, input current regulation takes over. An open ILIM floats above 0.8 V and limits input current to zero; a shorted ILIM leaves the register in charge. EN_ILIM = 0 turns off both limiting and monitoring on the pin.

In buck mode charge current is reduced to hold the junction at the TREG setting, 60°C to 120°C; termination is then suspended, the safety timer runs at half rate and THERM_STAT is high. Above TSHUT the converter and BATFET turn off, CHRG_FAULT reads 10 and INT pulses; they return below TSHUT_HYS. In boost mode, above TSHUT the BATFET turns off to stop discharge, and the host restores it with one of the BATFET-enable events once the temperature is below TSHUT_HYS.
Buck operation is for VBUS within VVBUS_OP. Above VACOV switching stops at once, CHRG_FAULT reads 01 and INT pulses.
On a load transient that drives SYS too high, the converter stops at once to clamp the overshoot.
If PMID rises past VOTG_OVP, switching stops and boost pauses (OTG_CONFIG stays set) until the fault clears; BOOST_FAULT is set and INT pulses.

Battery overvoltage is 4% above the regulation voltage; charging stops at once, BAT_FAULT is set and INT pulses. Below VBAT_DPL the BATFET opens to prevent over-discharge, and only an input on VBUS brings it back; the battery is then charged at IBATSHORT (100 mA typ) below VSHORT, or at IPRECHG between VSHORT and VBATLOWV. A shorted or badly overloaded system (above the BATFET overcurrent limit) latches the BATFET off until a BATFET-enable event.

Target address 6AH (1101010 plus R/W). Registers REG00 to REG14; a read past REG14 returns FFh, and an undefined register address is answered with NACK. Standard (100 kbit/s) and fast (400 kbit/s) modes. SDA and SCL are open drain and need pull-ups. The target may stretch the clock. Multi-byte reads and writes work across REG00 to REG14 except REG0C, which takes single reads only and holds faults until read; NTC_FAULT is the exception and always shows the present TS state.

After power-on reset the part is in default mode with the watchdog expired and all registers at defaults; it charges on its own with a 12 hour fast-charge timer, then stops charging while the buck keeps powering SYS. WATCHDOG_FAULT is high in default mode and low in host mode. Any I2C write enters host mode; the host must set WD_RST before the watchdog expires or set WATCHDOG = 00 to stay there. On expiry the part returns to default mode and resets every register to default; six settings survive: BATFET_DIS, BATFET_DLY, BATFET_RST_EN, IINLIM, VINDPM_OS and VINDPM.

Input capacitor: low-ESR X7R or X5R ceramic, as close as possible to the high-side drain and low-side source, rated 25 V or more for inputs up to 14 V; 8.2 µF suits 3 A to 5 A charging. Output: for loop stability 1 µH and at least 20 µF, ceramic X7R or X5R rated 6 V or more. A larger output LC lowers ripple.
SYS is powered from a 3.9 V to 14 V source on VBUS rated at least 100 mA, or from a single Li-ion cell above VBATUVLO on BAT. For full output power to SYS the source needs at least 3 A.

In order of priority: the input capacitor tight to PMID and GND with the shortest copper or a ground plane; the inductor right at SW, with that trace only as wide as the charge current needs, small in area, on one layer, and far from other copper; the output capacitor near the inductor and IC, grounded by short copper to the IC ground; analog and power ground routed apart and joined once, at the power pad under the IC or through a 0 Ω resistor; ground pour kept off power pins; decoupling capacitors at their pins with short traces; the exposed pad soldered to ground with thermal vias under the IC into the ground planes; vias sized and counted for the current they carry.
